Well, let me sit down and think about this year's plan. I'm 70 now, been on this same piece of ground for 50 years. My wife helps when she can, our son works in the city at a factory, sends some money back, and our daughter-in-law helps at harvest. So really it's mostly me in the field day to day. Five mu isn't much, but at my age, it's about right — any more and I couldn't keep up.

I do wheat and maize, same as always. The land can support both, and if one does poorly, the other usually carries us. I'm not about to try something new at my age — cotton used to be big around here but it's too much work now, and vegetables need hands I don't have.

**Winter wheat (already in the ground from last October, but let me explain how I planned it):**

I planted around October 12th, same as every year, right after the maize came off. Used Jimai 22 seed from the agri-supply shop in town — about 15 jin per mu, costs me around 30 yuan per mu. I still save a little from my own harvest for backup but mostly buy fresh seed now, the yields are better.

For base fertilizer I put down compound 15-15-15, about a bag (40 kg) per mu before the rotary tiller went through. That's roughly 6 kg of N per mu from the base. The extension guy at the township station says you should do soil testing, but I've farmed this plot so long I know it's on the heavier clay side and takes fertilizer well. At jointing in March, I'll topdress urea — probably about 15 kg per mu, which gives me another 7 kg of N. So about 13-14 kg N total per mu. Some of my neighbors do more, 18 or 20, but urea prices are high this year and I don't want to overdo it.

Irrigation — my well still works, shared with two other households. Winter water (dong shui) I did in late November. Then I'll water at jointing end of March, again at heading in April, and probably one more at grain-filling if May is dry. Three or four times total. Each watering costs me maybe 25-30 yuan per mu in pumping — the electricity adds up.

For pests and weeds, I'll put down a herbicide in early spring, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray once. Nothing fancy.

Expected yield: maybe 900-950 jin per mu (450-475 kg/mu). Last year I got about 920 jin, year before was a bit less because of that late frost. I'd be happy with 900.

**Summer maize (will plant in June after wheat harvest):**

As soon as the combine comes through in mid-June — I hire the combine, 80 yuan per mu, not going to swing a sickle at 70 — I'll have the custom planter put in maize directly into the stubble. No tillage between. That's become normal around here, the window is too tight otherwise, maybe 4-5 days. I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, about 40 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer for maize I do a bit less — base 30 kg of compound at planting, plus urea topdress at the big trumpet stage (about knee-high) around 15-18 kg per mu. Maize responds well to the topdress. Total N about 12-13 kg per mu.

Irrigation depends on the rain. Usually June-August gets enough rain, but if it's dry at tasseling I'll water once, maybe twice. Last two years I only watered once.

Pesticide — I'll put herbicide down after planting, and watch for corn borer in August. If I see damage I spray.

Yield expectation: around 1000 jin per mu (500 kg/mu). Maize has been doing well, and the rain usually cooperates in summer.

**Money side of it:**

I'm careful with cash. My son sends money but I don't want to depend on it for farm inputs. Between seed, fertilizer, pumping, herbicide, and the custom combine and planter, I spend maybe 700-750 yuan per mu for wheat and 450-500 for maize. Over 5 mu both seasons, that's around 6000 yuan in inputs for the year. I could probably squeeze more yield by fertilizing more or watering a fourth time on maize, but the extra yuan in doesn't always come back as yuan out, especially with grain prices where they are.
